summary: Former Mark Twain National Forest tower on Lime Kiln Mountain near Hilda, Taney County. A 1954 survey describes a steel tower about 50 ft high; no source describes the site now.

facts.design: Four-legged steel tower with an open crow's nest
facts.status_note: Wikipedia calls it the former Hilda Lookout Tower; no source gives a removal date or describes what remains.

events.note: Coast and Geodetic Survey station description records the steel tower, about 50 feet high, with an open crow's nest

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1954 survey gives 1.5 miles south of the Hilda post office. Wikipedia gives approximately one mile south on Lime Kiln Mountain, with no starting point. The two may use different reference points, but both put the site south of Hilda.

sources.title: Hilda - Forest Lookouts (National Geodetic Survey station description GF0739 as reproduced)

notes_for_editor: The 1954 description is read from the Central US Lookouts page, which reproduces the National Geodetic Survey datasheet GF0739; I did not open the NGS datasheet itself. The status is now 'unknown' (it was 'gone'). Wikipedia's word 'former' suggests the tower is no longer there, but Wikipedia gives no removal date and cites a 1967 USGS quadrangle I did not open. A second source or a date would firm it up. The record's point lies south of the community, consistent with the survey. Do not confuse this with Hilda, Mississippi (Jackson County), a different fire tower on the Eastern US Lookouts page (data/raw/eastern_us_lookouts/hilda.html), which is not used here. The WebSearch budget ran out after my first search for this site; I did not run a second search or any workaround. Search snippets were not cited. Access is unknown.
